findings.where: Step 7 'Mid-height bars' text, and explain paragraph 2 ('Textbooks call this the [[mid-ordinate rule]] ... add up a graph you have only as readings')
findings.what: The mid-ordinate rule's name and its use on readings have no source in the lesson, and 'Textbooks call this' credits a source nobody cites. The research notes already hold the MCA quote ('Determines the area of an indicator card using the mid-ordinate rule', notes 3.5/3.6), so cite it and say his MCA papers call it that.

Two claims are untrue as written. 'However close the readings' is wrong because a spike is caught once readings are closer together than the spike lasts, and the analogy itself says the log closes in on the meter. 'Nothing hides between the bars' is wrong because a smooth rule can hide a narrow bump between bars at any given count. The honest break is that the meter gives F by measuring it, while a rate given as a rule needs the reverse rule to find F, and a log of readings has no rule to reverse, so bars are all it allows.

Why the bars settle on F(b) − F(a) is given only in words ('each thin bar is very nearly how much the charge rises across it'). The picture shows only c cancelling. Drawing each bar's amount as a step up the t³ + c curve (a staircase that hugs it) would let him see the cause.

findings.where: Step 5 and step 3 SHOW text at 360 px
findings.what: Step 5 puts F, F(b) − F(a), a and b, c cancelling, why the bars agree and 'definite integral' into one paragraph of about 120 words, and step 3 runs about 110 words. On a phone the graph and slider sit below the fold, so the 3.6 s and 4.6 s demonstrations play while he is still reading. Shorten them, or split step 5 in two.

The ∫ sign with its two ends never appears on a screen. ∫₀² 3t² dt is only in the explain text, but his HN papers set definite integrals that way (SQA 'one indefinite and one definite integral'). Add it to step 5's working rows and to one puzzle's wording, for example step 6 as ∫₁² 3t² dt.

findings.where: Graph labels, step 1 ('i = 3 A') and step 2 ('v = 5 m/s')
findings.what: Labels inside the graph set i and v upright, while the title above sets them in italics. flushLabels strips the backticks before K.labels, so the italics are lost.
A boat on v = t² reaches 36 m/s (about 70 knots) in 6 s. Even labelled as an example, that will look wrong to a marine reader. Make it a car, or use a gentler rule.
'Slide the bars up to 100' asks him to do what the demonstration has just done for him. Say 'then drag the slider yourself' so the control reads as his to play with.
The right answer is the middle button in 4 of the 7 puzzles. Spread it more evenly across the three positions.
